newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriot leader urges talks after shooting.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriot leader urges talks after shooting.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on Monday urged Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides to hold talks with him after a Turkish Cypriot soldier was shot dead near the U.N.-patrolled buffer zone at the weekend.
Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller told journalists in Ankara that she would travel to Cyprus for Tuesday's funeral of Allahverdi Kilic, 20, the victim of the shooting.

"I call on Mr Clerides to meet and to talk with me either at his palace, here, or at the residence of U.N. permanent representative Gustave Feissel," Denktash told reporters in the Turkish Cypriot sector of Nicosia.
"We have to talk in order to cool off the heat and tension," said Denktash, head of a self-proclaimed Turkish Cypriot state.

He blamed the Cypriot government for Sunday's shooting, in which another soldier was wounded. He described the assailants as "two professionals wearing civilians clothes who used professional means and who escaped to the (Greek Cypriot) south".
The Cyprus government has categorically denied Greek Cypriot involvement in the incident.

"The National Guard had absolutely no involvement," government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides told reporters in the Greek Cypriot sector of the capital. "Police did not detect suspicious movements or given any indication that Greek Cypriots are to blame," he said.

The Cypriot government will only consent to a meeting with Denktash once agreement has been achieved on a number of points connected to the Cyprus problem through proximity talks, Cassoulides said. Such common ground will ensure a successful political dialogue to breach the impasse, he said.
In Ankara, Ciller warned the Greek Cypriots would "not get out of this easily" if it was established that they had deliberately fired shots.
"We can't give this up. We'll continue to try and get to the bottom of this," she told reporters at the foreign ministry.
Kilic's funeral will be held in Nicosia after midday prayers. It will be Ciller's second visit to the breakaway state in a month.
Inquiries into the shooting are being carried out by the Turkish Cypriot forces in the north, with assistance from police of the British base of Dhekelia, near where it took place.
"It will take a miracle to crack this one," said a source close to the inquiry.

Tensions have risen in the last month following the killing of the two Greek Cypriots by security forces and civilians in the Turkish-occupied areas during demonstrations against the division of the island.
The island has been divided since Turkish troops invaded 22 years ago after a short-lived coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
